title: Production Launch Checklist
subtitle: Every item to verify before going live — security, performance, monitoring, backups, and the final pre-launch walkthrough

content.text: Aviation uses checklists not because pilots are incompetent, but because humans forget things under pressure. Launching a product involves dozens of steps, many of which interact with each other. A single missed step — HTTPS redirect not enabled, error tracking not configured, backups pointing at the wrong database — can cost you users, data, or credibility. This checklist covers everything we've learned in this track, organized as a pre-launch runthrough.

content.code:
HTTPS:
  [ ] HTTPS enabled — no HTTP-only responses
  [ ] HTTP → HTTPS redirect (301) is configured
  [ ] HSTS header set (Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000)
  [ ] Certificate is valid and auto-renews

HEADERS:
  [ ] X-Frame-Options: DENY (or SAMEORIGIN if embedding needed)
  [ ] X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
  [ ] Content-Security-Policy configured (prevents XSS injection)
  [ ] Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
  [ ] Permissions-Policy set (disable unused browser features)

SECRETS:
  [ ] No secrets in git history (check: git log -p | grep -i secret)
  [ ] .env NOT committed (check: git ls-files | grep .env)
  [ ] .env.example committed with empty values
  [ ] Production secrets stored in platform secrets manager
  [ ] Different secrets for staging vs production

AUTHENTICATION:
  [ ] Password hashed with bcrypt/argon2 (NEVER plain text or MD5)
  [ ] JWT secrets are long (32+ random bytes), not 'mysecret'
  [ ] Session tokens are httpOnly cookies (not localStorage for auth)
  [ ] Rate limiting on login endpoint (prevent brute force)
  [ ] CSRF protection on state-changing endpoints

DATABASE:
  [ ] Database not exposed to internet (only accessible from app server)
  [ ] DB user has minimum required permissions (not superuser)
  [ ] SQL queries use parameterized queries (prevent SQL injection)

STATIC ASSETS:
  [ ] Gzip/Brotli compression enabled on Nginx or CDN
  [ ] CSS and JS minified (Vite does this in production build)
  [ ] Images compressed and in modern format (WebP, AVIF)
  [ ] Cache-Control: immutable, max-age=31536000 on hashed assets
  [ ] Cache-Control: no-cache on index.html

CDN:
  [ ] Static files served from CDN (Cloudflare, CloudFront, Vercel Edge)
  [ ] CDN configured for your domain (not origin-only serving)

DATABASE:
  [ ] Indexes on all foreign keys
  [ ] Indexes on columns used in WHERE clauses (check query plan)
  [ ] N+1 query problem absent (use eager loading, not per-row queries)
  [ ] Database connection pooling enabled

PAGE SPEED:
  [ ] Lighthouse score: Performance > 80 (run: npm run build && serve -s dist)
  [ ] LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) < 2.5 seconds
  [ ] CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) < 0.1
  [ ] Bundle size checked: npm run build (Vite shows sizes)
  [ ] No unused dependencies included in bundle

content.filename: Monitoring: be the first to know
content.code:
UPTIME:
  [ ] Uptime monitoring configured (BetterStack, UptimeRobot)
  [ ] Health check endpoint (/health) responding with 200
  [ ] Alert goes to email AND Slack (or phone for critical apps)
  [ ] Status page configured (optional but professional)

ERROR TRACKING:
  [ ] Sentry (or equivalent) initialized in both frontend and backend
  [ ] Error alerts configured (notify on new issues)
  [ ] Source maps uploaded for readable stack traces
  [ ] User context set in Sentry (so you know which users are affected)

LOGGING:
  [ ] Structured JSON logging enabled
  [ ] Logs being stored somewhere queryable (not just stdout)
  [ ] Request IDs added to all log lines
  [ ] Sensitive data NOT being logged (passwords, tokens, card numbers)
  [ ] Log retention policy set (auto-delete after 30-90 days)

BACKUPS:
  [ ] Automated database backup scheduled (at minimum: daily)
  [ ] Backup restoration has been TESTED (not just configured)
  [ ] Backup files stored outside the production server
  [ ] Recovery runbook documented

content.filename: Adding all security headers in Express

content.code:
BEFORE LAUNCH (1-2 days before):
  [ ] Deploy to staging and test all critical flows manually
  [ ] Run Lighthouse audit on staging
  [ ] Confirm all environment variables are set in production
  [ ] Test sending an alert (verify Slack/email notifications work)
  [ ] Take a database backup and test restoration
  [ ] Review error tracking — resolve any pre-existing errors

LAUNCH DAY:
  [ ] Deploy latest build to production
  [ ] Verify health check is green
  [ ] Walk through critical user flows:
      - Sign up / login
      - Core feature (make a purchase, submit a form, etc.)
      - Error state (invalid input, 404 page)
  [ ] Check error tracking: no new errors immediately post-deploy
  [ ] Check uptime monitoring: green status
  [ ] Verify DNS, HTTPS, redirects all working

POST-LAUNCH (24 hours after):
  [ ] Review error tracking for any new issues users encountered
  [ ] Review logs for any suspicious patterns
  [ ] Check database query performance (any slow queries?)
  [ ] Confirm backups have been running
  [ ] Take note of real traffic patterns for capacity planning

EMERGENCY ROLLBACK:
  [ ] Documented: how to roll back to previous version
  [ ] Previous version's Docker image or git tag recorded
  [ ] Everyone who can deploy knows how to roll back

content.text: Check your security headers at securityheaders.com after launch. Enter your domain and get an instant grade (A+ to F) with explanations for what's missing. Mozilla Observatory (observatory.mozilla.org) gives a more detailed security scan including CORS policy, cookie settings, and CSP analysis. Both are free. An A or A+ grade means your headers are correctly configured. Aim for at least a B before launch.

questions.question: You launch your app and users report that navigating to pages directly gives a 404 error, but the homepage loads fine. What checklist item did you miss?
options: SPA routing rule not set — server needs to serve index.html for all paths (/* → /index.html 200)
CDN cache needs to be purged
questions.explanation: This is the classic SPA routing bug. React Router handles routes in JavaScript — but the JavaScript only runs after index.html loads. When a user navigates directly to '/dashboard', the server looks for a file at that path and finds nothing, returning 404. The fix: configure your server to serve index.html for all paths that don't match actual files. In Nginx: 'try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html'. In Netlify: '/* /index.html 200' in _redirects. This should be in your checklist under frontend routing configuration.

faq.q: How long should a production launch take with this checklist?
faq.a: For a new app: the security and performance items take 2-4 hours to implement the first time. After that, subsequent launches take 30 minutes for the day-of checklist. The monitoring and backup setup is one-time work. For an experienced team, everything on this checklist is standard practice that's built into the development workflow — you're not adding it at launch, you're verifying it's in place.

examples: Helth startup breaches consistently trace back to items on this list: hardcoded secrets, missing HTTPS, no rate limiting on auth endpoints. The OWASP Top 10 (10 most common security vulnerabilities) is essentially a list of 'items missed on this checklist'. Companies spending millions on security still get breached due to basics like missing headers or exposed secrets

High-profile launches (Product Hunt launches, HN Show HN posts) often expose bugs that only surface under real traffic. Teams that go through a launch checklist systematically — especially testing critical flows on staging — avoid the most painful launch-day incidents
